## Statement

[View PDF](pdf/main.pdf) · [Download LaTeX source](latex/main.tex) -- mirrors this page's placeholder statement; see [c/0004](/c/0004/) for the $k=1$ base case this generalizes.

### Setting

As in [c/0004](/c/0004/): fix nonempty finite $\mathcal{K}$ (seeds), $\mathcal{D}$ (inputs), $\mathcal{R}$ (outputs), $K = |\mathcal{K}|$, $D = |\mathcal{D}|$, $R = |\mathcal{R}|$. Take $k$ independent $\epsilon$-unpredictable sources $S_1, \dots, S_k$ over the same $(\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R})$, each producing its own $(x_i, z_i)$. Draw $k$ independent seeds $\mathit{sd}_1, \dots, \mathit{sd}_k \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{K}$ and reveal all of them publicly, alongside all of $H$ and all the $z_i$.

::: {.callout-note title="Definition ($k$-Instance Public-Seed Extraction)"}
For a challenge bit $b$, set $y_{i,0} \leftarrow H(\mathit{sd}_i, x_i)$ and $y_{i,1} \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{R}$ for each $i$, and let $\mathsf{D}$ output a guess $b'$ given $H$, all $\mathit{sd}_i$, all $y_{i,b}$, and all $z_i$. Define
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub\text{-}}k}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S_1,\dots,S_k,\mathsf{D}) := 2\Pr[b'=b] - 1 .
$$
:::

### The Placeholder Conjecture

::: {.callout-note title="Fact (trivial hybrid bound, not in question)"}
By a standard hybrid argument over the $k$ instances, using [c/0004](/c/0004/)'s corollary at each step,
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub\text{-}}k}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S_1,\dots,S_k,\mathsf{D}) \;\le\; k \cdot \frac{8}{5}\Bigl( \sqrt{\epsilon R} + \sqrt{\tfrac{\log_2 D}{K}} \Bigr) .
$$
At $k=1$ this is exactly [c/0004](/c/0004/)'s corollary, which is why that statement `specializes` this one.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Conjecture (placeholder, untested)"}
The linear-in-$k$ factor above is not necessary: there is a bound of the same shape with the $k$-dependence replaced by $O(\sqrt{k})$ or better, exploiting that a single distinguisher must succeed jointly across all $k$ instances rather than being handed $k$ independent certificates.
:::
